decisions_and_interpretations.kind: DEVIATION from the literal pre-registration wording
decisions_and_interpretations.text: The pre-registration says 'days with any missing bar 15:19-15:59 are dropped'. Primary D1 day set = build_d1.py default `keep`, which treats a run of 1-4 no-update (flat, zero-volume) Dukascopy minutes as a valid carry-forward bar (runs >= 5 or starting 09:30 are missing). This is looser than the literal wording: the strict reading (`keep_strict`: any no-update minute in 15:19-15:59 counts as missing) drops 374 more days (mostly the sparse-feed years 2013-14 and 2017). Kept as primary because it was fixed before any H1/H2 number was computed and switching after seeing both results would itself be a post-hoc choice; the strict reading is reported in full for H1/H2 and gives the same H1/H2 conclusions.
decisions_and_interpretations.source: this analysis; relabelled from 'interpretation' to 'deviation' after audit finding 7

decisions_and_interpretations.text: S2 'best full-sample D1 t-stat' = the H2 predictor with the largest |Newey-West t| on the full D1 sample (as pre-registered); trade direction: buy the ATM call if sign(t) x P > 0, else (including P = 0) buy the ATM put, as the pre-registration's 'else ATM put' says. If the predictor is undefined (a bar it needs is missing) the day is excluded from the S2 mean, not booked as $0. Look-ahead check: the same selection repeated on D1 dates before the first D2 session is reported next to it.
decisions_and_interpretations.source: workflow clarification (labelled); zero/undefined handling changed after audit finding 3

decisions_and_interpretations.kind: DEVIATION forced by the no-look-ahead rule
decisions_and_interpretations.text: If P3 is the selected predictor its value is only known at the 15:51 open, so S2 enters at the 15:51 bar open (strike nearest SPX then) instead of the pre-registered t0 = 15:49 ('same entry/exit'). The other reading of the rule (best |t| among the predictors known at t0, i.e. P1/P2/P4, entering at 15:49) is reported next to it as 'S2-alt' with its own pass rule evaluation.
decisions_and_interpretations.source: this analysis; S2-alt added after audit finding 3

decisions_and_interpretations.text: The implied-vs-realized model is fitted on D1 days from 2023-01-01 up to the day before the first D2 session collected, so no D2 test day (or any day in the D2 window) is inside the fit that predicts it. Its out-of-sample calibration on D1 days inside the D2 window is reported.
decisions_and_interpretations.source: this analysis; added after audit finding 5 (before: fit ran through 2026-10-20)

decisions_and_interpretations.text: Pass-rule conditions are three-valued: yes / no / not evaluable. Condition 1 for S1/S3 needs a bootstrap CI over D2 days, so it is not evaluable with fewer than 2 usable D2 days. Condition 2 requires CIs to be reported, so it is not evaluable with fewer than 2 usable D2 days. A strategy is a candidate only if both are 'yes'; anything else is FAIL, and a FAIL caused by 'not evaluable' is labelled 'D2 test not run'.
decisions_and_interpretations.source: this analysis; added after audit findings 1 and 2

decisions_and_interpretations.text: The realized-move model is fitted to the D1 move to the 15:59 bar close (16:00:00), while the straddle settles on the SPX official close. In D2 the 15:59-close -> official-close gap averages about 1.3 bps in absolute value (exploratory (iii)), so the model slightly understates the move the option actually pays on; this works against the S1/S3 premise.
decisions_and_interpretations.source: this analysis; added after audit finding 9

decisions_and_interpretations.text: Robinhood option bar opens look like sampled prints/marks, not clean bid-ask mids (bar open is not the previous close; put-call parity is off by up to ~1.6 points at 15:49-15:50 on the one real day). If they are trade prints, adding a $0.10 half-spread may double-count part of the cost; if they are mids it is the right charge. Parity per usable day is reported as a data-quality line.
decisions_and_interpretations.source: this analysis; added after audit finding 4

decisions_and_interpretations.text: 11-minute window starting at bar s = open of bar s to close of bar s+10 (same length as r_close: 15:49:00-16:00:00). The 15:38 window is open 15:38 -> close 15:48. Same-day median uses every available window starting 10:00..15:38 (339 when no bar is missing).
Strike nearest SPX = nearest point on the 5-point grid, ties rounded up; the contract must have a real (non-interpolated) 1-minute bar at entry or the day is not usable.

Fees are charged per executed trade: entry always; exit only when a leg is sold before expiry (cash settlement is not a trade). Half-spread is added to the entry mark and subtracted from a sale price; settlement value is intrinsic at the SPX official close.

S3 / exploratory (i): a leg is sold at multiple x entry mark minus half-spread (floored at 0) if the close of any real bar beginning 15:49..15:58 is >= multiple x entry mark (the 15:49 bar's close at 15:49:59 is later than the 15:49:00 entry).
decisions_and_interpretations.source: this analysis (reading of 'any later bar's close ... before 15:59')

decisions_and_interpretations.text: Realized vol to t0 = sqrt(sum of squared 1-minute log changes of bar opens 09:30..15:49, rescaled for missing pairs), from D1 on the D2 date. Model fitted on D1 2023-01-01 .. the day before the first D2 session: |P_end/P_t0 - 1| = a + b*rv (OLS). Predicted move (points) = prediction x SPX at t0; compared with the D2 15:49 ATM straddle mark (C+P open). Pass-rule statistic = mean over usable D2 days of (predicted - implied); 95% CI from a day bootstrap that resamples D1 days (refitting, 20-day moving blocks) and D2 days (iid). The ratio model (sum|r|/sum rv) and the unconditional mean are reported as descriptive alternatives.
decisions_and_interpretations.source: this analysis (pre-registration says 'ratio and regression'; workflow asked for the regression)

decisions_and_interpretations.text: Day-block bootstrap for every D1 resample = circular moving-block bootstrap with blocks of 20 consecutive trading days (keeps volatility clustering), 10000 replications, percentile 95% CI, seed 20261021; the 1-day-block (iid) version is reported as a sensitivity. Samples of D2 trades (<= ~35 days) are resampled iid, since a 20-day block on 22 days would leave almost nothing to resample. For the implied-vs-realized premise the CI must lie above zero under BOTH the 20-day-block and the iid D1 resample (conservative: for the regression the block CI is narrower than the iid one, because the regression score has lag-1 autocorrelation of about -0.76, driven by back-to-back extreme-volatility days).
decisions_and_interpretations.source: this analysis; block length changed 1 -> 20 after audit finding 6

decisions_and_interpretations.text: An extra fee case of $1.13 per contract per side (upper end of Robinhood's actual SPXW fee: contract fee + exchange fee + regulatory, research/SPX_1549_RESEARCH.md section F) is added to the cost grid as a labelled, not pre-registered sensitivity.
decisions_and_interpretations.source: this analysis; added after the literature review
